MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MAY 31, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-I9) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Smith called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith and Commissioners Jeffrey Jennings, John
  Mazza and Mark Wetton

  ABSENT: Chair Kraig Hill

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Assistant City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works
  Director; Raneika Brooks, Senior Planner, Courtney McCammon, City Biologist; Patricia
  Salazar. Senior Administrative Analyst; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Chair Hill absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on May 25, 2022.

ITEM 1  NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Malibu Middle and High School Specific Plan Final Environmental Impact
  -

  Report No. 20-001. Local Coastal Pro~rarn Amendment No. 21-002. General

  modernize the existing Malibu Middle and High School campus and former Juan
  Cabrillo Elementary School campus
  Location:  30215 Morning View Drive, within the appealable coastal zone
  APNs:  4469-017-900. 4469-018-900. and 4469-018-904
  Owner:  Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District
  Case Planner: Senior Planner Brooks, 456-2489, ext. 276
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-40 making
  a recommendation to the City Council on the adequacy of the Final Environmental
  Impact Report (SCH No. 202008350), the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
  Program, and the Statement of Overriding Considerations; and Local Coastal
  Program Amendment No. 2 1-002 adding the Malibu Middle and High School
  Campus Specific Plan to the Local Coastal Program and corollary amendments
  including General Plan Map Amendment No. 2 1-002, Zoning Map Amendment
  No. 22-001, and Zoning Text Amendment No. 22-002 (Santa Monica-Malibu
  Unified School District)

RECUSED:  Commissioner Jennings recused himself due to proximity to the proposed
  development and left the meeting at 6:35 PM.

  Assistant City Attorney Rusin noted that the Planning Commission would consider
  a legislative item, review the proposed specific plan, entitlements and
  Environmental Impact Report and make recommendations to the City Council.
  Coastal Development Permits would be presented to the Planning Commission at a
  future date.

  Disclosures:  Commissioners Mazza, Wetton and Vice Chair Smith

  Senior Planner Brooks presented the staff report.

  The Commission directed questions to staff.

  As there were no further questions for staff~ Vice Chair Smith opened the public
  comment section of the public hearing.

  Speakers: Steve Massetti, Carey Upton, Rachel Stowell, Bill Sampson, Robert
  Brinkrnan. Isaac Burgess, Stacy Rouse, Cohn Drummond, Craig Foster. Jo
  Drummond, Roui Israel, Carl Randall. Caren Leib, Kim Ford, Valerie Seabaugh,
  Lou LaMonte, Marianne Riggins, Chiarmaine Mark, Bessie Zhang. Sue Murphree,
  Adam Friedman, Howard Rudzki, Michael Burke, Seth Jacobson

  The applicant team declined rebuttal to public comment.

  As there were no other speakers present, Vice Chair Smith closed the public
   Malibu Planning Commission

  Page 3 of 3

  comment portion of the public hearing and returned the matter to the table for
  discussion.

  The Commission discussed the project and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Wetton seconded a motion to
  adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-40 as amended, 1) City performs
  monitoring functions proposed by the Environmental Impact Report; 2) Public
  Works Department complete the traffic review prior to the City Council hearing; 3)
  the Dark Sky Ordinance applies to the whole campus including the pool; 4)
  electronic messaging signs should face toward the school rather than toward the
  street, be limited to five feet in height, and required to be turned off one half hour
  following the last scheduled event; 5) all public entrances to the school for
  pedestrian and auto access shall be taken off Morning View Drive and parking Lot
  F shall thereby be eliminated; 6) denying staff’s recommendation to remove the
  grading quantities for phases 2-4; and 7) making a recommendation to the City
  Council on the adequacy of the Final Environmental Impact Report (SCH No.
  202008350), the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program, and the Statement
  of Overriding Considerations; and Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 2 1-002
  adding the Malibu Middle and High School Campus Specific Plan to the Local
  Coastal Program and corollary amendments including General Plan Map
  Amendment No. 21-002, Zoning Map Amendment No. 22-001, and Zoning Text
  Amendment No. 22-002 (Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District)

  The question was called and the motion carried 3-0, Chair Hill and Commissioner
  Jennings absent.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 11:01 p.m., Commissioner Wetton moved and Commissioner Mazza seconded
  a motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.
  Approved and adopted by the Planning Commission
  of the City o Malibu on September 5, 2023.

  SK~J,AR PEAK, Planning Commission Chair
